q24827.en: It is advisable for a driver who shows signs of tiredness to reach the nearest lay-by and rest.

explain.short: A tired driver reacts slowly and may fall asleep. Stopping in a safe place and resting is the right choice.
explain.rule: Tiredness slows your reactions and attention. The only cure is to stop in a safe place and rest.
explain.trap: 'la più vicina piazzola' (the nearest lay-by): stop as soon as you can, do not push on.

sceneParams.caption: Tired? Stop at the nearest lay-by and rest

keywords.en: lay-by (small parking area by the road)

q24828.en: It is advisable for a driver who shows signs of tiredness to get as close as possible to the vehicle in front.

explain.short: A tired driver reacts more slowly, so they need MORE space in front, not less. The right thing is to stop and rest.
explain.rule: Tiredness slows your reactions and attention. The only cure is to stop in a safe place and rest.
explain.trap: 'avvicinarsi il più possibile' (get as close as possible) is the opposite of safe: tiredness needs a bigger gap.

sceneParams.caption: Tired: never tailgate, stop and rest
lines: Close to the car ahead: crash

keywords.en: to get as close as possible

q24829.en: Some hours must pass before a driver who has drunk too much alcohol becomes fit to drive again.

explain.short: The body removes alcohol slowly. Only time, several hours, brings the driver back to normal.
explain.rule: The body removes alcohol slowly, over several hours. Nothing you eat or drink makes it faster.
explain.trap: 'alcune ore' (some hours) is correct: there is no quick fix.

sceneParams.caption: Only time removes alcohol: some hours

q24830.en: A driver who has drunk too much alcohol cannot quickly become fit to drive again, especially if they have also taken medicines.

explain.short: Alcohol leaves the body slowly. Many medicines add to its effect, so recovery takes even longer.
explain.rule: The body removes alcohol slowly, over several hours. Nothing you eat or drink makes it faster.
explain.trap: 'non può... velocemente' (cannot quickly) is correct, and 'specie se... farmaci' makes it even worse.

sceneParams.caption: No quick recovery, worse with medicines

q24831.en: A driver who has drunk too much alcohol can quickly become fit to drive again by eating rather salty food.

explain.short: Salty food does not remove alcohol from the blood. Only time does that.
explain.rule: The body removes alcohol slowly, over several hours. Nothing you eat or drink makes it faster.
explain.trap: 'velocemente' (quickly) with 'cibi salati' (salty food) is a myth: no food makes you sober.

sceneParams.caption: Salty food does not remove alcohol

q24832.en: A driver who has drunk too much alcohol can quickly become fit to drive again by drinking black coffee.

explain.short: Coffee may make you feel awake, but the alcohol is still in your blood. Only time removes it.
explain.rule: The body removes alcohol slowly, over several hours. Nothing you eat or drink makes it faster.
explain.trap: 'caffè amaro' (black coffee) is the classic myth: it does not make you sober.

sceneParams.caption: Coffee does not remove alcohol

q24833.en: Fitness to drive can be impaired by using some sedative medicines.

explain.short: Sedatives calm the brain and can make you sleepy. That makes driving unsafe.
explain.rule: Substances that act on the brain (alcohol, drugs, some medicines) can make you unfit to drive. Normal drinks and supplements do not.
explain.trap: 'alcuni farmaci sedativi' (some sedative medicines): read the leaflet, many cause drowsiness.

sceneParams.caption: Sedatives can make you sleepy

q24834.en: Fitness to drive can be impaired by using antidepressant medicines.

explain.short: Antidepressants act on the brain and can cause drowsiness or slower reactions. They can make driving unsafe.
explain.rule: Substances that act on the brain (alcohol, drugs, some medicines) can make you unfit to drive. Normal drinks and supplements do not.
explain.trap: 'antidepressivi' are medicines, but they can still affect driving: check the leaflet and ask the doctor.

sceneParams.caption: Antidepressants can affect driving
lines: Read the leaflet, ask the doctor

q24835.en: Fitness to drive can be impaired by using hallucinogens (LSD, ecstasy, etc.).

explain.short: Hallucinogens change what you see and feel. Driving under drugs is dangerous and forbidden.
explain.rule: Substances that act on the brain (alcohol, drugs, some medicines) can make you unfit to drive. Normal drinks and supplements do not.
explain.trap: 'allucinogeni (LSD, ecstasy)' are drugs: they always affect driving.

sceneParams.caption: Drugs like LSD and ecstasy: no driving

keywords.en: hallucinogens (drugs that change what you see)

q24836.en: Fitness to drive can be impaired by using alcoholic drinks.

explain.short: Alcohol slows reactions, narrows your field of vision and gives false confidence. It makes driving unsafe.
explain.rule: Substances that act on the brain (alcohol, drugs, some medicines) can make you unfit to drive. Normal drinks and supplements do not.
explain.trap: 'bevande alcoliche': the limit is 0.5 g/l, and ZERO for new drivers (first 3 years), drivers under 21 and professional drivers.

sceneParams.caption: Alcohol impairs driving
lines: Limit 0.5 g/l, zero for new drivers

q24837.en: Fitness to drive can be impaired by using black coffee.

explain.short: Coffee does not damage your ability to drive. It is not a drug or a sedative.
explain.rule: Substances that act on the brain (alcohol, drugs, some medicines) can make you unfit to drive. Normal drinks and supplements do not.
explain.trap: 'caffè amaro' (black coffee) is harmless here; but remember it also does not cancel alcohol.

sceneParams.caption: Coffee does not impair driving
lines: Not a drug, not a sedative

q24838.en: Fitness to drive can be impaired by using fizzy drinks.

explain.short: Fizzy drinks (without alcohol) do not affect the brain. They do not make you unfit to drive.
explain.rule: Substances that act on the brain (alcohol, drugs, some medicines) can make you unfit to drive. Normal drinks and supplements do not.
explain.trap: 'bevande gassate' (fizzy drinks) sound like 'bevande alcoliche', but they are harmless.

sceneParams.caption: Fizzy drinks do not impair driving

q24839.en: Fitness to drive can be impaired by using mineral salt supplements.

explain.short: Mineral salt supplements only give the body salts it needs. They do not affect driving.
explain.rule: Substances that act on the brain (alcohol, drugs, some medicines) can make you unfit to drive. Normal drinks and supplements do not.
explain.trap: 'integratori di sali minerali' (mineral salt supplements) are not medicines that cause drowsiness.

sceneParams.caption: Mineral salts do not impair driving

q24840.en: Fitness to drive can be impaired by using food supplements.

explain.short: Food supplements are not drugs or sedatives. They do not make you unfit to drive.
explain.rule: Substances that act on the brain (alcohol, drugs, some medicines) can make you unfit to drive. Normal drinks and supplements do not.
explain.trap: 'integratori alimentari' (food supplements) are harmless here.

sceneParams.caption: Food supplements do not impair driving
lines: Not a drug, not a sedative

q24841.en: Taking hashish or marijuana can impair the ability to drive.

explain.short: Hashish and marijuana slow reactions and change how you see distances and time. Driving becomes unsafe.
explain.rule: Drugs change how you see, think and react. Driving after taking drugs is forbidden.
explain.trap: 'può compromettere' (can impair) is correct: every drug can affect driving.

sceneParams.caption: Hashish and marijuana impair driving

q24842.en: Taking heroin or cocaine can impair the ability to drive.

explain.short: Heroin and cocaine change reactions, attention and judgement. Driving after taking them is dangerous and forbidden.
explain.rule: Drugs change how you see, think and react. Driving after taking drugs is forbidden.
explain.trap: 'può compromettere' (can impair) is correct: every drug can affect driving.

sceneParams.caption: Heroin and cocaine impair driving

q24843.en: Sedative medicines contain some substances that can impair the ability to drive.

explain.short: Sedatives contain substances that calm the brain and can cause drowsiness. That can make driving unsafe.
explain.rule: Drugs change how you see, think and react. Driving after taking drugs is forbidden.
explain.trap: 'alcune sostanze' (some substances): not every medicine, but sedatives can affect driving. Read the leaflet.

sceneParams.caption: Sedatives can make you drowsy

q24844.en: Taking LSD or amphetamine does not impair the ability to drive.

explain.short: LSD and amphetamines are drugs: they change what you see and how you judge risk. They DO impair driving.
explain.rule: Drugs change how you see, think and react. Driving after taking drugs is forbidden.
explain.trap: 'non compromette' (does not impair) is the lie: every drug impairs driving.

sceneParams.caption: LSD and amphetamines DO impair driving

keywords.en: LSD (a drug that changes what you see)

q24845.en: Taking hashish or marijuana does not impair the ability to drive.

explain.short: Hashish and marijuana are drugs: they slow reactions and change how you see distances. They DO impair driving.
explain.rule: Drugs change how you see, think and react. Driving after taking drugs is forbidden.
explain.trap: 'non compromette' (does not impair) is the lie: 'light' drugs also impair driving.

sceneParams.caption: Hashish and marijuana DO impair driving

q24846.en: A heavy and excessive meal is not recommended for someone who has to drive.

explain.short: A big, heavy meal makes you sleepy and less alert. Before driving, eat light.
explain.rule: Before driving, eat light meals and do not drink alcohol. A full stomach does not cancel alcohol.
explain.trap: 'sconsigliata' (not recommended) is correct: heavy food and driving do not mix.

sceneParams.caption: Before driving, eat light

q24847.en: Eating food that is hard to digest can cause a drop in attention and longer reaction times.

explain.short: Digesting heavy food takes a lot of energy and makes you drowsy. You notice danger later and react later.
explain.rule: Before driving, eat light meals and do not drink alcohol. A full stomach does not cancel alcohol.
explain.trap: 'aumento dei tempi di reazione' (longer reaction times) means SLOWER reactions, which is correct.

sceneParams.caption: Hard-to-digest food: slower reactions

keywords.en: food that is hard to digest

q24848.en: Drinking spirits during a large meal does not impair the ability to drive.

explain.short: Spirits are strong alcohol. Food may slow how fast alcohol enters the blood, but it still impairs driving.
explain.rule: Before driving, eat light meals and do not drink alcohol. A full stomach does not cancel alcohol.
explain.trap: 'durante un pasto abbondante' (during a large meal) does not cancel the alcohol: 'non compromette' is wrong.

sceneParams.caption: Spirits impair driving, even with a meal

q24849.en: Alcohol can cause a state of euphoria, which leads to underestimating danger.

explain.short: Alcohol makes you feel happy and sure of yourself. You think risks are smaller than they really are.
explain.rule: Alcohol slows reactions and gives false confidence. Drunk driving is a crime that can lead to arrest; the rules apply to every driver of a vehicle.
explain.trap: 'euforia' (euphoria) means false confidence: you feel great but drive worse.

sceneParams.caption: Alcohol: false confidence, danger ignored

q24850.en: Anyone who drives while drunk risks arrest.

explain.short: Driving drunk is a crime in Italy. At higher alcohol levels the law gives arrest, as well as fines and licence suspension.
explain.rule: Alcohol slows reactions and gives false confidence. Drunk driving is a crime that can lead to arrest; the rules apply to every driver of a vehicle.
explain.trap: 'rischia l'arresto' (risks arrest) is correct: the penalty can include arrest, not only a fine.

sceneParams.caption: Drunk driving can lead to arrest

q24851.en: It is not advisable to drive when you are in an altered emotional state.

explain.short: Strong anger, sadness or worry take your mind off the road. Your attention and judgement get worse.
explain.rule: Alcohol slows reactions and gives false confidence. Drunk driving is a crime that can lead to arrest; the rules apply to every driver of a vehicle.
explain.trap: 'stato emotivo alterato' (upset emotional state) counts as a condition that affects driving.

sceneParams.caption: Upset or angry? Better not to drive

q24852.en: Anyone who rides a vehicle without an engine with a blood alcohol level above the set limit is not subject to any penalty.

explain.short: The drink-driving rules apply to anyone driving a vehicle, also a bicycle. So there IS a penalty.
explain.rule: Alcohol slows reactions and gives false confidence. Drunk driving is a crime that can lead to arrest; the rules apply to every driver of a vehicle.
explain.trap: 'senza motore' (without an engine) does not mean no rules: 'non è soggetto ad alcuna sanzione' is wrong.

sceneParams.caption: On a bike over the limit: still a penalty

keywords.en: vehicle without an engine (e.g. a bicycle)

q24853.en: Anyone who drives while drunk has faster reaction times.

explain.short: Alcohol makes reactions SLOWER, not faster. The drunk driver brakes later and covers more distance before stopping.
explain.rule: Alcohol slows reactions and gives false confidence. Drunk driving is a crime that can lead to arrest; the rules apply to every driver of a vehicle.
explain.trap: 'più rapidi' (faster) is the lie: alcohol slows you down even if you feel quick.

sceneParams.caption: Alcohol makes reactions slower, not faster

q24854.en: Helping someone injured on the road is required by law.

explain.short: Every road user must help a person injured in a road accident. Not helping is punished.
explain.rule: Every road user must help injured people after an accident. It is a legal duty, not only a moral one.
explain.trap: 'obbligatorio per legge' (required by law) is correct: it is a legal duty for everyone.

sceneParams.caption: Helping the injured is a legal duty

q24855.en: Helping someone injured on the road can mean saving their life.

explain.short: In the first minutes after an accident, simple help (calling 112, stopping bleeding) can keep the person alive.
explain.rule: Every road user must help injured people after an accident. It is a legal duty, not only a moral one.
explain.trap: 'può significare salvargli la vita' (can mean saving their life) is correct: quick help matters.

sceneParams.caption: Quick help can save a life

q24856.en: Helping someone injured on the road straight away can prevent them from suffering further physical harm.

explain.short: Acting fast, for example pressing on a wound or protecting the person from traffic, stops things from getting worse.
explain.rule: Every road user must help injured people after an accident. It is a legal duty, not only a moral one.
explain.trap: 'subito' (straight away) and 'ulteriori danni' (further harm): quick help limits the damage.

sceneParams.caption: Quick help prevents further harm

q24857.en: Helping someone injured on the road is not a duty imposed by law, only a moral duty.

explain.short: Helping the injured IS a legal duty, not just a moral one. Not helping is punished by law.
explain.rule: Every road user must help injured people after an accident. It is a legal duty, not only a moral one.
explain.trap: 'solo un dovere morale' (only a moral duty) is wrong: it is required by law.

sceneParams.caption: Helping is a legal duty, not only moral

keywords.it: non è un obbligo imposto dalla legge
keywords.en: is not a duty imposed by law

q24858.en: You must help someone injured on the road only if you think the accident is serious.

explain.short: You must help any injured person, whatever you think of the accident. You cannot judge the injuries yourself.
explain.rule: Every road user must help injured people after an accident. It is a legal duty, not only a moral one.
explain.trap: 'solo se' (only if) is the trap: the duty does not depend on how serious you think it is.

sceneParams.caption: Help every injured person, not only in bad crashes

q24859.en: You do not have to help someone injured on the road if doing so blocks traffic.

explain.short: Saving a person is more important than traffic flow. Blocking traffic is no excuse for not helping.
explain.rule: Every road user must help injured people after an accident. It is a legal duty, not only a moral one.
explain.trap: 'intralcio alla circolazione' (blocking traffic) is not a reason to skip the legal duty.

sceneParams.caption: Traffic jam is no excuse: help the injured

q24860.en: Helping someone injured on the road is required only for doctors and health workers.

explain.short: The duty to help is for everyone, not only for medical staff. Anyone can call 112 and give simple first aid.
explain.rule: Every road user must help injured people after an accident. It is a legal duty, not only a moral one.
explain.trap: 'solo per i medici' (only for doctors) is the trap: the law applies to all road users.

sceneParams.caption: Everyone must help, not only doctors

q24861.en: You do not have to help someone injured on the road, so as not to put your own safety at risk.

explain.short: Helping is required. You must protect yourself while you help (hazard lights, warning triangle, high-visibility vest), but you cannot simply refuse.
explain.rule: Every road user must help injured people after an accident. It is a legal duty, not only a moral one.
explain.trap: 'per non mettere a repentaglio la propria sicurezza' (so as not to risk your safety) is not a general excuse: help safely.

sceneParams.caption: Help the injured, but protect yourself too

q24862.en: The aim of first aid is to try to keep the injured person alive with simple, immediate actions.

explain.short: First aid is not medical treatment. It means simple things done at once to keep the person alive until help comes.
explain.rule: First aid keeps the injured person alive and safe until help arrives. Call 112, do only simple things, and avoid anything harmful.
explain.trap: 'semplici e immediati' (simple and immediate) describes first aid exactly.

sceneParams.caption: First aid: simple, quick actions to keep alive

q24863.en: The aim of first aid is to look after the injured person as well as possible while waiting for medical help to arrive.

explain.short: You are not a doctor: you help the person as best you can and keep them safe until the ambulance comes.
explain.rule: First aid keeps the injured person alive and safe until help arrives. Call 112, do only simple things, and avoid anything harmful.
explain.trap: 'in attesa che arrivi il soccorso medico' (while waiting for medical help): first aid comes before the doctors.

sceneParams.caption: Look after the injured until help arrives

keywords.en: to look after the injured person

q24864.en: During first aid you must avoid, as far as possible, further harm to the injured person.

explain.short: A good helper protects the person from more harm: from traffic, from wrong movements, from cold.
explain.rule: First aid keeps the injured person alive and safe until help arrives. Call 112, do only simple things, and avoid anything harmful.
explain.trap: 'ulteriori danni' (further harm): the first rule is 'do no more harm'.

sceneParams.caption: First aid: avoid any further harm

q24865.en: During first aid you must avoid wrong or harmful actions being done to the injured person.

explain.short: Well-meant but wrong actions can hurt the person. Do only simple things you know are safe.
explain.rule: First aid keeps the injured person alive and safe until help arrives. Call 112, do only simple things, and avoid anything harmful.
explain.trap: 'interventi sbagliati o dannosi' (wrong or harmful actions) must be avoided: correct.

sceneParams.caption: Avoid wrong or harmful actions

q24866.en: The aim of first aid is to ask the injured person straight away how the accident happened.

explain.short: First aid is about keeping the person alive, not about finding out what happened. The police deal with that.
explain.rule: First aid keeps the injured person alive and safe until help arrives. Call 112, do only simple things, and avoid anything harmful.
explain.trap: 'chiedere come è avvenuto l'incidente' (ask how it happened) is not first aid.

sceneParams.caption: First aid is not asking questions

keywords.en: to ask the injured person straight away

q24867.en: During first aid you must move the injured person away from where they are in every case.

explain.short: Moving an injured person can make injuries worse, for example to the spine. Move them only if there is danger, like fire.
explain.rule: First aid keeps the injured person alive and safe until help arrives. Call 112, do only simple things, and avoid anything harmful.
explain.trap: 'in ogni caso' (in every case) is the trap: move them only when they are in danger.

sceneParams.caption: Do not move the injured unless there is danger

q24868.en: During first aid you must never touch the injured person if the police have not yet arrived.

explain.short: You do not need to wait for the police to help. Simple first aid, like pressing on a wound, must start at once.
explain.rule: First aid keeps the injured person alive and safe until help arrives. Call 112, do only simple things, and avoid anything harmful.
explain.trap: 'mai... se non è ancora arrivata la polizia' (never... before the police arrive) is wrong: helping does not wait for the police.

sceneParams.caption: Help at once, no need to wait for police

q24869.en: If someone injured on the road has a bleeding wound, you must cover it with sterile material, or material as clean as possible, to stop the bleeding.

explain.short: Covering the wound with clean material and pressing helps the blood stop and keeps germs out.
explain.rule: Cover and press the wound with clean material. Leave stuck objects in place. Never give drinks to an unconscious person.
explain.trap: 'sterile o quanto più possibile pulito' (sterile or as clean as possible): use the cleanest thing you have.

sceneParams.caption: Cover the wound with clean material
lines: Cover with sterile or clean cloth

q24870.en: If someone injured on the road has a bleeding wound that is dirty with soil, you must wash it as soon as possible with clean water.

explain.short: Soil carries germs. Washing the wound with clean water lowers the risk of infection; then cover it.
explain.rule: Cover and press the wound with clean material. Leave stuck objects in place. Never give drinks to an unconscious person.
explain.trap: 'acqua pulita' (clean water) is the key: only clean water, not hot water.

sceneParams.caption: Dirty wound: wash with clean water

q24871.en: During first aid, if the injured person has a bleeding wound with foreign objects stuck in it, you must not remove them from the wound.

explain.short: An object stuck in a wound may be blocking the blood. Pulling it out can cause heavy bleeding and more damage.
explain.rule: Cover and press the wound with clean material. Leave stuck objects in place. Never give drinks to an unconscious person.
explain.trap: 'non bisogna toglierli' (you must not remove them) is correct: leave stuck objects for the doctors.

sceneParams.caption: Never pull out objects stuck in a wound

q24872.en: If someone injured on the road has a bleeding wound, you must pad it with sterile gauze or clean cloths.

explain.short: Pressing sterile gauze or a clean cloth on the wound helps to stop the blood.
explain.rule: Cover and press the wound with clean material. Leave stuck objects in place. Never give drinks to an unconscious person.
explain.trap: 'tamponarla' (pad it, press on it) is the right action for a bleeding wound.

sceneParams.caption: Press sterile gauze or a clean cloth on it

keywords.en: to pad it, to press on it

q24873.en: During first aid, if the injured person has a bleeding wound, you must immediately remove any foreign objects in it and then cover the wound.

explain.short: Objects stuck in a wound must stay in place: pulling them out can cause heavy bleeding. Cover around them and wait for help.
explain.rule: Cover and press the wound with clean material. Leave stuck objects in place. Never give drinks to an unconscious person.
explain.trap: 'togliere subito gli eventuali corpi estranei' (remove the objects at once) is the mistake.

sceneParams.caption: Leave stuck objects in the wound

q24874.en: If someone injured on the road has a bleeding wound and is unconscious, you must give them water or tea to drink.

explain.short: Never give drinks to an unconscious person: they cannot swallow and may choke.
explain.rule: Cover and press the wound with clean material. Leave stuck objects in place. Never give drinks to an unconscious person.
explain.trap: 'incosciente' (unconscious) + 'dargli da bere' (give them a drink) is dangerous: they could choke.

sceneParams.caption: Unconscious: never give anything to drink

q24875.en: If someone injured on the road has a bleeding wound, you must not cover it, so the blood can stop on its own.

explain.short: A bleeding wound must be covered and pressed with clean material. Leaving it open lets blood and germs flow freely.
explain.rule: Cover and press the wound with clean material. Leave stuck objects in place. Never give drinks to an unconscious person.
explain.trap: 'non bisogna coprirla' (you must not cover it) is the mistake: always cover a bleeding wound.

sceneParams.caption: Always cover and press a bleeding wound

keywords.en: the blood stopping on its own

q24876.en: If someone injured on the road has a bleeding wound, you must pour hot water on it to stop the bleeding.

explain.short: Hot water does not stop bleeding and can hurt the person. Press on the wound with clean material instead.
explain.rule: Cover and press the wound with clean material. Leave stuck objects in place. Never give drinks to an unconscious person.
explain.trap: 'acqua calda' (hot water) is the mistake: only clean water to wash, then cover and press.

sceneParams.caption: No hot water: cover and press

q24877.en: If someone injured on the road has heavy external bleeding, you must pad the wound and call for help at once.

explain.short: Heavy bleeding is life-threatening. Press on the wound to slow the blood and call 112 straight away.
explain.rule: Stop the blood by pressing on the wound, call 112 and keep the person still, sitting or lying down.
explain.trap: 'tamponare... e chiamare subito i soccorsi' (pad and call for help at once): both actions are right.

sceneParams.caption: Press the wound and call 112 at once

keywords.en: to call for help at once

q24878.en: If someone injured on the road has heavy external bleeding, you must pad the wound at once, pressing on it with clean or, if possible, sterile material.

explain.short: Firm pressure with clean material is the best way to slow heavy bleeding until help arrives.
explain.rule: Stop the blood by pressing on the wound, call 112 and keep the person still, sitting or lying down.
explain.trap: 'facendo pressione' (pressing) is the key: pressure stops the blood.

sceneParams.caption: Press hard with clean or sterile material

q24879.en: If someone injured on the road has heavy external bleeding, you must try to stop the blood from flowing out.

explain.short: Losing a lot of blood can kill. Stopping the flow, by pressing on the wound, is the first job.
explain.rule: Stop the blood by pressing on the wound, call 112 and keep the person still, sitting or lying down.
explain.trap: 'arrestare la fuoriuscita del sangue' (stop the blood flowing out) is exactly the goal.

sceneParams.caption: Heavy bleeding: stop the blood

keywords.en: to stop the blood flowing out

q24880.en: If someone injured on the road has heavy external bleeding, it is advisable, if possible, to place them sitting or lying down while waiting for help to arrive.

explain.short: A person losing blood may faint. Sitting or lying down keeps them still and safe from a fall.
explain.rule: Stop the blood by pressing on the wound, call 112 and keep the person still, sitting or lying down.
explain.trap: 'posizione seduta o sdraiata' (sitting or lying down) is right; making them walk would be wrong.

sceneParams.caption: Keep them sitting or lying down
lines: Sit or lie the person down

keywords.it: in attesa che arrivino i soccorsi
keywords.en: while waiting for help to arrive

q24881.en: If someone injured on the road has heavy external bleeding, you must only dress the wound.

explain.short: Dressing the wound is not enough: you must also press to stop the blood and call for help at once.
explain.rule: Stop the blood by pressing on the wound, call 112 and keep the person still, sitting or lying down.
explain.trap: 'solo' (only) is the trap: one action is not enough.

sceneParams.caption: Not only dress it: press and call 112

q24882.en: If someone injured on the road has heavy external bleeding, you must cover the wound and make the injured person walk.

explain.short: Walking makes the heart pump more blood out of the wound, and the person may faint. Keep them still.
explain.rule: Stop the blood by pressing on the wound, call 112 and keep the person still, sitting or lying down.
explain.trap: 'far camminare' (make them walk) is the mistake: they must sit or lie down.

sceneParams.caption: Never make a bleeding person walk
lines: Sit or lie down, stay still

keywords.en: to make the injured person walk

q24883.en: If someone injured on the road has heavy external bleeding, you absolutely cannot give them water to drink.

explain.short: The quiz treats 'absolutely' as too strong: the strict ban on drinks is for an unconscious person. A conscious person who loses blood gets thirsty, and the official answer allows small sips of water.
explain.rule: Stop the blood by pressing on the wound, call 112 and keep the person still, sitting or lying down.
explain.trap: 'assolutamente' (absolutely) is the trap word: the rule is not absolute for a conscious person.

sceneParams.caption: 'Absolutely no water' is too strong

q24883.reviewNote: Official answer FALSE; modern first-aid guidance usually advises giving nothing to drink to a person with heavy bleeding (may need surgery). Explained via the absolute word 'assolutamente'.

q24884.en: If a foreign object (a splinter of glass, wood or other) has got into the eye of someone injured on the road, you must bandage the eye, without doing anything else.

explain.short: Trying to remove the object can damage the eye. A bandage stops the person touching it until a specialist helps.
explain.rule: Bandage the eye and wait for a specialist. Never try to remove the object yourself.
explain.trap: 'senza procedere ad altre manovre' (without doing anything else) is correct: only bandage.

sceneParams.caption: Something in the eye: bandage, nothing else
lines: Glass or wood in the eye

q24885.en: If a foreign object has got into the eye of someone injured on the road, you must advise them not to touch the injured eye, to avoid more damage.

explain.short: Rubbing or touching the eye can push the object deeper. Tell the person to keep their hands away.
explain.rule: Bandage the eye and wait for a specialist. Never try to remove the object yourself.
explain.trap: 'non toccare l'occhio' (do not touch the eye) is correct advice.

sceneParams.caption: Tell them not to touch the eye
lines: Do not touch or rub it

keywords.en: not to touch the injured eye

q24886.en: If a foreign object has got into the eye of someone injured on the road, you must bandage the eye, avoiding touching it until the specialist arrives.

explain.short: Only a specialist should remove an object from the eye. Your job is to bandage it and leave it alone.
explain.rule: Bandage the eye and wait for a specialist. Never try to remove the object yourself.
explain.trap: 'fino all'intervento dello specialista' (until the specialist arrives): you do not try to fix it yourself.

sceneParams.caption: Bandage the eye, leave it to the specialist

q24887.en: If a foreign object has got into the eye of someone injured on the road, you must always try, no matter what, to remove it.

explain.short: Removing an object from the eye can cause serious damage. Leave it to the specialist and only bandage the eye.
explain.rule: Bandage the eye and wait for a specialist. Never try to remove the object yourself.
explain.trap: 'sempre e comunque' (always, no matter what) is the trap: never try to remove it yourself.

sceneParams.caption: Never try to remove it yourself
lines: Do not try to remove it

q24888.en: If a foreign object has got into the eye of someone injured on the road, you must make them keep their eyes open, to avoid other injuries.

explain.short: Forcing the eyes open does not help and can cause more damage. Bandage the eye instead.
explain.rule: Bandage the eye and wait for a specialist. Never try to remove the object yourself.
explain.trap: 'costringerlo a tenere gli occhi aperti' (force them to keep their eyes open) is wrong.

sceneParams.caption: Do not force the eyes open: bandage

q24889.en: If a foreign object has got into the eye of someone injured on the road, you must gently massage their eyelid, to help tears flow.

explain.short: Massaging the eyelid can scratch the eye or push the object deeper. Do not touch: bandage it.
explain.rule: Bandage the eye and wait for a specialist. Never try to remove the object yourself.
explain.trap: 'massaggiargli delicatamente la palpebra' (gently massage the eyelid) sounds kind but is harmful.

sceneParams.caption: No massage: bandage the eye

q24890.en: If a foreign object has got into the eye of someone injured on the road, you must never bandage the injured eye.

explain.short: Bandaging the eye is exactly the right action: it protects the eye until a specialist arrives.
explain.rule: Bandage the eye and wait for a specialist. Never try to remove the object yourself.
explain.trap: 'non bisogna mai bendargli' (you must never bandage) is the opposite of the correct rule.

sceneParams.caption: Bandaging the eye is right

q24891.en: Shock shows as very pale and cold skin.

explain.short: In shock, blood goes away from the skin to the vital organs. So the skin becomes very pale and cold.
explain.rule: Shock = pale, cold, sweaty skin, shivers and a fast heartbeat. Think 'pale and cold', never 'red and hot'.
explain.trap: 'pelle molto pallida e fredda' (very pale, cold skin) is a classic sign of shock.

sceneParams.caption: Shock: very pale, cold skin

q24892.en: Shock shows as cold sweat on the forehead.

explain.short: Cold sweat, especially on the forehead, is a typical sign of shock.
explain.rule: Shock = pale, cold, sweaty skin, shivers and a fast heartbeat. Think 'pale and cold', never 'red and hot'.
explain.trap: 'sudore freddo' (cold sweat) is a classic sign of shock.

sceneParams.caption: Shock: cold sweat on the forehead

q24893.en: Shock shows as shivers, very pale skin and cold sweat on the forehead.

explain.short: Shivers, very pale skin and cold sweat together are the typical picture of shock.
explain.rule: Shock = pale, cold, sweaty skin, shivers and a fast heartbeat. Think 'pale and cold', never 'red and hot'.
explain.trap: All three ('brividi, pelle molto pallida, sudorazione fredda') are real signs of shock.

sceneParams.caption: Shock: shivers, pale skin, cold sweat

q24894.en: Shock shows as very pale skin, cold sweating and a fast heartbeat.

explain.short: In shock the heart beats fast to push blood around. Pale skin and cold sweat come with it.
explain.rule: Shock = pale, cold, sweaty skin, shivers and a fast heartbeat. Think 'pale and cold', never 'red and hot'.
explain.trap: 'frequenti battiti del cuore' (fast heartbeat) is also a sign of shock.

sceneParams.caption: Shock: pale, cold sweat, fast heartbeat

q24895.en: Shock can show as suddenly saying sentences and words that make no sense.

explain.short: Shock reduces blood to the brain, so the person may become confused and say things that make no sense.
explain.rule: Shock = pale, cold, sweaty skin, shivers and a fast heartbeat. Think 'pale and cold', never 'red and hot'.
explain.trap: 'può manifestarsi' (can show): confusion is a possible sign, not always present.

sceneParams.caption: Shock can cause confused speech

q24896.en: Shock always shows as a strong rise in body temperature.

explain.short: Shock makes the skin cold, not hot. A high temperature (fever) is not a sign of shock.
explain.rule: Shock = pale, cold, sweaty skin, shivers and a fast heartbeat. Think 'pale and cold', never 'red and hot'.
explain.trap: 'sempre' (always) and 'aumento della temperatura' (rise in temperature) are both wrong: shock means cold skin.

sceneParams.caption: Shock: cold skin, not fever

q24897.en: Shock shows as large dark spots on the skin.

explain.short: In shock the skin becomes very pale, not covered in dark spots.
explain.rule: Shock = pale, cold, sweaty skin, shivers and a fast heartbeat. Think 'pale and cold', never 'red and hot'.
explain.trap: 'ampie macchie scure' (large dark spots) is not a sign of shock: think 'pale'.

sceneParams.caption: Shock: pale skin, not dark spots

q24898.en: Shock shows as red skin and strong hot flushes.

explain.short: Red, hot skin is the opposite of shock. In shock the skin is pale and cold.
explain.rule: Shock = pale, cold, sweaty skin, shivers and a fast heartbeat. Think 'pale and cold', never 'red and hot'.
explain.trap: 'colorito rosso' and 'vampate di calore' (red colour, hot flushes) are the opposite of shock.

sceneParams.caption: Shock: pale and cold, not red and hot
